finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST parameter `feed` is passed straight to file_get_contents() with no authentication, scheme allowlist, host check, or IP check. Because file_get_contents accepts PHP stream wrappers (http, https, ftp, file, php://, phar://, data:, etc.), the attacker can reach internal HTTP services and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and can probe local files. The response is not reflected, but its byte length is echoed. That leaks a size oracle, internal-port and host probing through timing and errors, and file existence and size through file://. phar:// can additionally trigger deserialization.

trace.note: Gate checks only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']). There is no require_admin() call and no login check.
The attacker-controlled value is passed unmodified to file_get_contents(), which fetches it server-side.
echo strlen($xml) returns the fetched content length to the attacker, giving a size and existence oracle and enabling blind probing.

finding.guards_checked: No validation of any kind. There is no scheme or wrapper allowlist, no hostname allowlist or blocklist, and no DNS-resolved IP check. There is no authentication either: require_admin() is defined at line 4 but is not called on this path. There is no redirect restriction, since the http wrapper follows redirects by default. allow_url_fopen is assumed to be at its default of On.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen(), and require_admin() (defined at line 4) is only called at line 18 on a different branch, with no allowlist, scheme check or host check anywhere on the path.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: POST parameter `set_webhook` is passed to curl_init() and curl_exec() with no scheme, host or IP validation. The curl options set no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction, so curl's default protocols (file, gopher, dict, ftp, ldap and others, depending on the build) are reachable. The URL can target internal services and cloud metadata, and gopher:// allows raw-protocol pivots to Redis and similar. The response is not reflected (only 'ok' is echoed), so it is blind SSRF. Redirects are not followed because CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not set. Severity is reduced because an authenticated admin session is required, but in a multi-tenant context a tenant admin is a plausible attacker.
finding.sink: curl_exec($ch) on a handle created by curl_init($hook) at import.php:20-22

trace.note: require_admin() checks $_SESSION['is_admin'] only. This is the sole guard.
curl_init($hook) sets CURLOPT_URL to the attacker value.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() restricts the path to admin sessions, which limits the attacker pool but is not an SSRF control. There is no scheme allowlist: CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS / CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS_STR is not set. There is no host or IP allowlist and no post-DNS IP check, so the path is DNS-rebindable. The response body is discarded (RETURNTRANSFER with the result unused, then 'ok'), so the SSRF is blind only.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 (session is_admin check only); no URL, scheme or host validation
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18, so the source is admin-only rather than controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, and nothing in the code shows a multi-tenant setup.
